original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Formal F2[Q8] on two dirty scalar registers with paid labels x=i, x^{-1}=-i, y=j, y^{-1}=-j (24 generators), free scalar GL_2(F2) mixing normalized by augmentation, targets diag([z],[z]) and diag([xy],[yx]) with z=xyxy=x^2=y^2=-1; exact minimum paid-call counts. Changes the paid-label alphabet of CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1822 by adding the two inverses.
scope_change_reason: Instantiates the card's allowed variation 'a specified nonabelian operation family' as the quaternion group with an enlarged paid-label set. Predecessor #1822 (and its open-next question) fixes labels x,y only and leaves inverse labels open; this package answers that alphabet variant exactly.
bottleneck_link: Scoped negative: enlarging the Q8 paid alphabet by inverses does not compress the central-pair bill below four calls, so this bit-primitive alphabet still does not change the paid recursive profile. No kappa claim (bit side does not bind).
stop_rule: Complete BFS to depth 4 against the direct four-call upper bound for both pair endpoints; stop once each minimum is decided exactly. No pivot to r>=3 or other address groups.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json (minima, layer sizes, ball hashes, generators) and verify.py (two independent engines, GL closure, depth-3 miss, omission and mutated-target controls); written argument in README.md.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Is the exact minimum still 4 for diag([z],[z],[z]) at r=3 under the inverse-label alphabet (direct bill 6)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Three active roles with inverses tests whether sharing scales beyond pairs once the alphabet already includes x^{-1} and y^{-1}.
open_questions.first_step: Meet-in-the-middle over depth-3 balls with the 112-generator inverse-label alphabet at r=3; record layer digests and a memory cap.
open_questions.blocked_by: State-space growth; depth-5 coverage needs a meet, not a plain BFS.

open_questions.question: Does adding the remaining non-identity labels {+-k, -1} as paid units compress either pair target?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A still larger closed alphabet would decide whether any Q8-label enlargement below the full group can beat the direct bill.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate the 6*6=36-generator alphabet at r=2 against the same two targets with depth-3 miss / depth-4 hit receipts.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing technical; a bounded follow-up of the same shape.
